verses.sanskrit: सच्चिदानन्दरूपाय कृष्णायाक्लिष्टकर्मणे | नमो वेदान्तवेद्याय गुरवे बुद्धिसाक्षिणे ||
verses.transliteration: saccidānandarūpāya kṛṣṇāyākliṣṭakarmaṇe | namo vedāntavedyāya gurave buddhisākṣiṇe ||
verses.translation: Salutation to Krishna who is of the nature of Sat-Chit-Ananda (existence-consciousness-bliss), whose actions are effortless, who is known through Vedanta, who is the Guru, and the witness of all intelligence.
verses.hindi: सच्चिदानन्दस्वरूप, अक्लिष्टकर्मा, वेदान्त द्वारा जानने योग्य, गुरु और बुद्धि के साक्षी कृष्ण को नमस्कार।
verses.commentary: The Brahmavaivarta's opening salutation encodes its entire theology: Krishna is "saccidānanda-rūpa" — the very form of the three absolute qualities of Brahman (sat/existence, chit/consciousness, ananda/bliss). This is not metaphor — the Purana asserts that these three are not abstract attributes of a formless absolute but are the living reality of the personal Krishna. "Aklista-karma" — effortless action: Krishna's lila (cosmic play) is not labor but the natural overflow of infinite being. "Vedantavedya" — known through Vedanta: the formless Brahman of the Upanishads and the personal Krishna of bhakti are one reality approached through different paths.

verses.sanskrit: एकमेवाद्वितीयं ब्रह्म निर्गुणं परमार्थतः | सगुणं भक्तिसुलभं कृष्णाख्यं परमेश्वरम् ||
verses.transliteration: ekamevādvitīyaṃ brahma nirguṇaṃ paramārthataḥ | saguṇaṃ bhaktisulaṃbhaṃ kṛṣṇākhyaṃ parameśvaram ||
verses.translation: The one without a second, Brahman — in ultimate truth it is without qualities (nirguna). With qualities (saguna), easily approached through bhakti, it is known as Krishna, the supreme Lord.
verses.hindi: परमार्थ में ब्रह्म एकमेव अद्वितीय और निर्गुण है। भक्ति से सुलभ सगुण रूप में वही कृष्ण नाम से परमेश्वर कहलाता है।
verses.commentary: The Brahmavaivarta's elegant synthesis of the nirguna-saguna debate that divided Vedantic schools: both are true, both are the same reality. Nirguna Brahman (the formless absolute of Advaita Vedanta) and saguna Krishna (the personal God of bhakti) are not different entities — they are the same reality approached at different depths. "Bhaktisulaṃbha" — easily accessible through bhakti: the nirguna absolute is cognitively inaccessible to ordinary minds, but the same reality, wearing the form of Krishna, becomes approachable through love. The form is not a concession to weakness; it is grace.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वं खल्विदं कृष्णो न भूतं न भविष्यति | स एव सर्वशक्त्याढ्यः सर्वकारणकारणम् ||
verses.transliteration: sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ kṛṣṇo na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati | sa eva sarvaśaktyāḍhyaḥ sarvakāraṇakāraṇam ||
verses.translation: All this is indeed Krishna — there was nothing else, nor will there be. He alone, endowed with all powers, is the cause of all causes.
verses.hindi: यह सब कुछ कृष्ण ही है — न पहले कुछ और था, न भविष्य में होगा। वही सर्वशक्तिसम्पन्न, सभी कारणों का कारण है।
verses.commentary: "Sarvam khalvidam Krishna" — all this is indeed Krishna. This is the Brahmavaivarta's conscious echo of the Chandogya's "sarvam khalvidam brahma" — all this is Brahman. The substitution is theological: Brahman = Krishna. Not a restriction of the infinite into a particular form but an identification: the infinite absolute IS this personal, loving, playful presence. "Sarva-shaktyāḍhya" — endowed with all powers: the Prakriti Khanda elaborates that all the distinct powers of the cosmos (protection, abundance, wisdom, devotion) are aspects of Krishna's single infinite shakti.

verses.sanskrit: राधा कृष्णस्य परमा शक्तिः प्रेमस्वरूपिणी | तयोर्भेदो न विद्यते जले शीतलता यथा ||
verses.transliteration: rādhā kṛṣṇasya paramā śaktiḥ premasvarūpiṇī | tayorbhedo na vidyate jale śītalatā yathā ||
verses.translation: Radha is the supreme power of Krishna — of the nature of pure love. Between them there is no difference, just as there is no difference between water and its coolness.
verses.hindi: राधा कृष्ण की परम शक्ति हैं — प्रेमस्वरूपिणी। उन दोनों में कोई भेद नहीं है, जैसे जल और उसकी शीतलता में भेद नहीं।
verses.commentary: "Jale śītalatā yathā" — as water and its coolness. The most elegant metaphor in the Brahmavaivarta for the Radha-Krishna relationship. Water (jala) and coolness (śītalatā) are not two things — you cannot have water without its coolness being inherent in it, and you cannot have water's coolness without the water. Similarly, Krishna (the infinite consciousness) and Radha (the infinite love that is its essential nature) are not two entities in relationship — they are one reality in two inseparable aspects. This is not romantic love as an analogy for divine love — it is the claim that love (Radha/prema) is the very nature of consciousness (Krishna/Brahman).

chapters.title: Ganesha Khanda — The Cosmic Remover of Obstacles

verses.sanskrit: विघ्नेश्वरः प्रथमपूज्यः सर्वकार्येषु पूजितः | बुद्धिप्रदो विद्याप्रदः सिद्धिप्रदश्च सर्वदा ||
verses.transliteration: vighneśvaraḥ prathamapūjyaḥ sarvakāryeṣu pūjitaḥ | buddhiprado vidyāpradaḥ siddhipradaśca sarvadā ||
verses.translation: The Lord of obstacles is the first to be worshipped, honoured in all undertakings. He always bestows buddhi (intelligence), vidya (knowledge), and siddhi (accomplishment).
verses.hindi: विघ्नेश्वर सभी कार्यों में प्रथम पूजनीय हैं। वे सदा बुद्धि, विद्या और सिद्धि प्रदान करते हैं।
verses.commentary: "Prathamapūjya" — first to be worshipped. The Ganesha Khanda explains the cosmic logic behind this universal Hindu practice: Ganesha represents buddhi (discriminating intelligence) — the faculty that determines what is real from what is apparent, what is worth pursuing from what is a distraction, what action is appropriate from what is reactive. Beginning any undertaking without this faculty engaged is to proceed blindly. Ganesha is worshipped first not as a magical guarantee but as a reminder: before acting, activate intelligence.

chapters.title: Shrikrishna Janma Khanda — The Theology of Krishna

verses.sanskrit: कलौ कल्मषचित्तानां पापद्रव्योपजीविनाम् | विधि क्रियाविहीनानां गतिर्गोविन्दकीर्तनम् ||
verses.transliteration: kalau kalmaṣacittānāṃ pāpadravyopajīvinām | vidhi kriyāvihīnānāṃ gatirgovi ndakīrtanam ||
verses.translation: In Kali Yuga, for those with impure minds, those who subsist by sinful means, those devoid of ritual observance — their path is the chanting of Govinda's name.
verses.hindi: कलियुग में कलुषित चित्त वालों के लिए, पाप के साधनों से जीने वालों के लिए, विधि-क्रिया से रहित लोगों के लिए — गोविन्दकीर्तन ही गति है।
verses.commentary: The Brahmavaivarta's most democratic and radical statement: the chanting of Krishna's name is the path specifically for those who are impure, who have acted wrongly, who have failed at proper religious observance. This is not resignation to impurity — it is the teaching that grace is not proportional to merit. The Name is available to the most broken, the most failed, the most compromised. The Kali Yuga teaching across the Puranas converges on this point: when the conditions for the "proper" path are absent, the Name remains. "Govinda-kirtana" — singing the Name — is sufficient.

verses.sanskrit: अण्डं भूतं भविष्यं च भूतं वर्तमानमेव च | अण्डं ब्रह्माण्डमिति प्रोक्तं यत्र विश्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् ||
verses.transliteration: aṇḍaṃ bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ ca bhūtaṃ vartamānameva ca | aṇḍaṃ brahmāṇḍamiti proktaṃ yatra viśvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam ||
verses.translation: The egg is the past, the future, and the present. The egg is called Brahmanda — the cosmic egg — in which the universe is established.
verses.hindi: अण्ड भूत, भविष्य और वर्तमान है। अण्ड को ब्रह्माण्ड कहा गया है — जिसमें विश्व प्रतिष्ठित है।
verses.commentary: The Brahmavaivarta Purana's teaching on Brahmanda — the cosmic egg. The universe is not created from nothing but emerges from an original "egg" (anda) that contains all time — past, present, and future. This is the Shakta cosmology: the cosmos is not a linear creation but an eternal unfolding from a primordial unity. The Brahmanda is both the womb and the egg — the container and the contained.

verses.sanskrit: कृष्णः सर्वभूतानां हृदये संनिविष्टः | यो जानाति स पश्यति यो न जानाति न पश्यति ||
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭaḥ | yo jānāti sa paśyati yo na jānāti na paśyati ||
verses.translation: Krishna dwells in the heart of all beings. He who knows, sees; he who does not know, does not see.
verses.hindi: कृष्ण सभी प्राणियों के हृदय में निवास करते हैं। जो जानता है, वह देखता है; जो नहीं जानता, वह नहीं देखता।
verses.commentary: The Brahmavaivarta Purana declares that Krishna dwells in the heart of all beings — not in distant heavens but in the innermost center of every living being. The verse then states the paradox of recognition: knowledge is seeing, ignorance is blindness. Krishna is equally present in all hearts, but only those who know can see. The seeing is not visual but recognitional — the recognition of the presence that is always there.

verses.sanskrit: राधा कृष्णयोः एकत्वं परमं तत्त्वमुच्यते | यो राधाकृष्णयोरेकं जानाति स परां गतिम् ||
verses.transliteration: rādhā kṛṣṇayoḥ ekatvaṃ paramaṃ tattvamucyate | yo rādhākṛṣṇayorekaṃ jānāti sa parāṃ gatim ||
verses.translation: The oneness of Radha and Krishna is called the supreme truth. He who knows the unity of Radha and Krishna attains the supreme state.
verses.hindi: राधा और कृष्ण की एकता को परम तत्व कहा जाता है। जो राधा-कृष्ण की एकता जानता है, वह परम गति प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: The Brahmavaivarta Purana teaches the supreme truth of Radha-Krishna unity. Radha is not merely Krishna's consort but the embodiment of shakti — the divine feminine power that is inseparable from Krishna. "Rādhā kṛṣṇayoḥ ekatvam" — the oneness of Radha and Krishna — is the recognition that consciousness (Krishna) and energy (Radha) are one reality. This is not philosophical abstraction but the recognition that the divine is both the witnessing consciousness and the active power of love.

verses.sanskrit: कृष्णः साक्षात् परं ब्रह्म निर्गुणो निश्चलः शुद्धः | योगिनां हृदये नित्यं कृष्णो भवति साक्षात् ||
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇaḥ sākṣāt paraṃ brahma nirguṇo niścalaḥ śuddhaḥ | yogināṃ hṛdaye nityaṃ kṛṣṇo bhavati sākṣāt ||
verses.translation: Krishna is indeed the supreme Brahman — without qualities, unmoving, pure. In the hearts of yogins, Krishna is indeed present.
verses.hindi: कृष्ण साक्षात् परम ब्रह्म हैं — निर्गुण, निश्चल, शुद्ध। योगियों के हृदय में कृष्ण साक्षात् विराजमान हैं।
verses.commentary: The Brahmavaivarta Purana identifies Krishna with the supreme Brahman — nirguna (without qualities), nishcala (unmoving), shuddha (pure). This is the non-dual teaching: Krishna is not a deity among deities but the absolute reality itself. The verse then states that this absolute reality is present in the hearts of yogins — not as a distant abstraction but as immediate presence. The yogin's heart is the location where the absolute becomes accessible.

verses.sanskrit: यत्र नृत्यति गोविन्दो रासमण्डलमध्यगः | तत्र सर्वाणि तीर्थानि सर्वे देवाः सनातनाः ||
verses.transliteration: yatra nṛtyati govindo rāsaṃaṇḍalamadhyagaḥ | tatra sarvāṇi tīrthāni sarve devāḥ sanātanāḥ ||
verses.translation: Where Govinda dances at the centre of the Rasa circle — there are all the sacred tirthas, there are all the eternal gods.
verses.hindi: जहाँ गोविन्द रासमण्डल के मध्य में नृत्य करते हैं — वहाँ सभी तीर्थ हैं, वहाँ सभी सनातन देव हैं।
verses.commentary: The Rasa lila — Krishna dancing with the gopis in the Vrindavana forest — is one of the most theologically dense images in the entire Bhakti tradition. The Brahmavaivarta's interpretation: the Rasa circle is the cosmos itself. Krishna at the centre is the supreme consciousness. Each gopi is an individual soul. The dance is the relationship between consciousness and all its manifestations — simultaneously intimate (each gopi feels Krishna is dancing with her alone) and universal (he is with all simultaneously). "Tatra sarvāṇi tīrthāni" — all sacred places are there: the Rasa is not in Vrindavana two thousand years ago; it is happening now, here, wherever genuine love of the divine is present.
